clue.text: Sign dry drink tipped over

indicators.note: something tipped over ends up the other way round, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: sec = dry, of wine
a sip is a small drink

explanation.surface: Someone knocks over a glass of dry wine.
explanation.walkthrough: SEC is the wine-list word for dry. The sign is a zodiac sign, not a road sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Pisces, the fish, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: I buy and sell just the way I want

parts.note: I stays as it is
to deal is to buy and sell

explanation.surface: A trader boasts of doing business entirely on their own terms.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one sentence; the break falls after 'sell', and 'I' does double duty in the surface as the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ideal is exactly as you would wish it.

clue.text: Descend from there, dear Lord!

definitions.meaning: literally, get down off the thing you are on

explanation.surface: Someone begs a climber to get down from somewhere dangerous.
explanation.walkthrough: One phrase, two readings: a literal order to climb down, and the idiom that scoffs at a claim.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Come off it!' and 'dear Lord!' are both cries of incredulity; read literally it tells someone to get down.

clue.text: Son regularly in temper

parts.note: S = son, as in genealogies
often = regularly

explanation.surface: A father complains that his boy keeps losing his temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Temper' looks like a noun for anger; here it is the verb meaning to moderate.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to temper anger or criticism is to make it milder.

clue.text: Wet blanket for Arctic swimmer?

definitions.meaning: taken literally, a fish in freezing water

explanation.surface: A spoilsport is likened to a creature from icy seas.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical second reading: a fish living in Arctic water is literally cold.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold fish is an aloof, unemotional person, much like a wet blanket who dampens any fun.

clue.text: Character scratching head after a ticking off — me, say?

indicators.note: the second part comes after the first

parts.note: a ticking off is an exchange of cross (angry) words
LETTER, a character, without its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone puzzled and scratching their head after being told off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scratching head' suggests puzzlement, but it strips the L from LETTER. 'Me' is the setter speaking of themself, hence 'say?'.
explanation.definitionFit: The 'me' of the clue is whoever wrote it: a crossword setter.

clue.text: Machine tool, scarlet, washed

parts.note: a lathe turns wood or metal
scarlet is a red

explanation.surface: A list describing a red machine tool that has been cleaned.
explanation.walkthrough: The commas make it read like an inventory; the definition is simply the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: Lathered means covered in soapy foam, as when washed.

clue.text: Bone in bird between fulmar's wings

indicators.note: in, read with between, says the bird is set inside the pair of outer letters
between means the bird sits in the gap between those two letters
the wings of a word are its two outer letters

parts.note: a fulmar is a seabird; the possessive only ties it to wings, so the word itself is fulmar
the emu is a large flightless Australian bird

explanation.surface: A bone found in a bird, lodged between the wings of a fulmar.
explanation.walkthrough: The fulmar is a grey-and-white seabird, which keeps the whole clue in an ornithologist's notebook; its 'wings' are just F and R, and 'in' and 'between' set EMU inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: The femur is the thigh bone, the longest bone in the human body.

clue.text: Bitterly sliced through by the wind

indicators.note: a blade slicing through something ends up inside it

parts.note: sourly = bitterly
THE stays as it is

explanation.surface: A bitter wind that cuts right through you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bitterly' and 'wind' seem to go together as a cold blast; in fact 'the wind' splits, with THE going into the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by category: air blowing up from the south is one kind of wind.

clue.text: Frozen ground melted for stream along with pond, initially

indicators.note: melting loses the shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: these nine letters are melted, along with the P, into a new order

indicators.note: 'initially' means at the start, so only the start of the word, its first letter, is used

parts.note: first letter of POND

explanation.surface: Frozen ground thaws into streams and ponds.
explanation.walkthrough: The irony is that permafrost is ground that never melts.
explanation.definitionFit: Permafrost is ground that stays frozen all year round.

clue.text: Claw measured, as unusually long, first of all

indicators.note: the first letter of all the words that follow

parts.note: first letters of Measured As Unusually Long

explanation.surface: A claw is measured and found to be unusually long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First of all' sounds like 'to begin with' but means the first letter of each word.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain verb synonyms: an animal that claws its prey tears at it savagely.

clue.text: Dropped bricks in underwear!

definitions.meaning: to drop a brick is to make a gaffe; a bloomer is a blunder

explanation.surface: Bricks tumble out of someone's knickers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop a brick' is British slang for making an embarrassing blunder, and a bloomer is the same thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloomers are both gaffes and loose women's knickers.

clue.text: Tray he soiled, dirty

indicators.note: something soiled has been messed up, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: TRAY HE rearranged

explanation.surface: A man has made a mess of a tray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soiled' and 'dirty' look like one idea repeated; the first is the instruction, the second the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses match: smelling of soil, and crude or bawdy, the sense of a dirty joke.

clue.text: Idle brain

definitions.meaning: a verb here: to laze about doing nothing
rhyming slang for the head, from a word that rhymes with bread

explanation.surface: A lazy mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loaf' for head comes from rhyming slang, loaf of bread = head; 'use your loaf' means think.
explanation.definitionFit: The first is a plain verb synonym for lazing about; the second is rhyming slang, loaf of bread for head, hence the brain.

clue.text: Remove from power with open question about king

parts.note: overt = open

indicators.note: one thing goes around another

parts.note: how is a question word
R = rex, king

explanation.surface: Rebels plot to depose a monarch by raising an open question about him.
explanation.walkthrough: R for king is from the Latin rex.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: toppling a ruler or government, usually by force.

clue.text: Cook's stuff lost on weaver

indicators.note: letters that are lost have lost their way, so the two words that follow are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A cook's belongings have gone missing and been pinned on a textile worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' rearranges the eight letters of ON WEAVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovenware is cookware such as dishes and casseroles made to withstand heat in a stove.

clue.text: Ferocious beast, furious lover tucked into Chardonnay, say

indicators.note: tucked into means the jumbled letters are placed inside the word for the drink

parts.note: Chardonnay is an example of wine, as the word say signals

indicators.note: furious means wild and agitated, so the letters of lover are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: An angry lover hides away inside a glass of white wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'furious' rearranges LOVER to OLVER, which is 'tucked into' WINE.
explanation.definitionFit: The wolverine is a stocky carnivore of northern forests famed for its strength and aggression.

clue.text: Original butcher ate rice, starter of venison put away

indicators.note: put away means the letter is stowed inside the rearranged letters, as food is put away by eating
to butcher something is to hack it up, so these letters are cut into a new order
the starter of a word is its first letter

parts.note: only the first letter of venison is used

explanation.surface: A butcher ate rice and polished off a venison starter too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butcher' looks like the cook, but it is the anagram signal, and 'put away' is the eating sense turned into an instruction to stow a letter inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Creative work is original and imaginative, showing fresh invention, so the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Overhaul due, after getting promoted

indicators.note: to overhaul something is to strip it down and rebuild it, so the letters of the two words are reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A worker is told their long-awaited service review is finally due now that they have been promoted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overhaul' rearranges DUE together with AFTER; 'after' looks like a link word, but its letters are part of the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A product or star that is featured is given special prominence, highlighted or publicised in a show or advert.

clue.text: Places in lounge discussed?

indicators.note: something discussed is spoken, so we want a sound

parts.note: to laze is to lounge

explanation.surface: Spots in a lounge that people talk about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Places' looks like a noun; it is the verb, as in lays a book on the table, and 'lounge' is a verb too.
explanation.definitionFit: To place something is to lay it down.

clue.text: Pieced together puzzle understood, some steps taken to start it

indicators.note: this piece goes at the front

parts.note: a jig is a lively dance, a set of steps
'I saw' = I understood

explanation.surface: Someone finally grasps a puzzle and takes steps to begin it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pieced together' is part of the definition: a jigsaw is a puzzle you piece together.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: a picture cut into interlocking shapes that the solver reassembles.

clue.text: Contribution from Gaia, the nature goddess

indicators.note: a contribution is a part of the whole, so the answer is part of the words

parts.note: gaiA THE NAture

explanation.surface: Something given by Gaia, the Greek earth goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: Gaia is herself a goddess, which makes her the tempting answer; she only houses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the Greek deity of wisdom is one goddess among many.

clue.text: Classic place bagged by sheep sometimes

indicators.note: to bag something is to capture it, so the answer is caught inside the letters of the words that follow

parts.note: shEEP SOMetimes

explanation.surface: A place that sheep sometimes graze.
explanation.walkthrough: The classics are England's five great flat horse races; two, the Derby and the Oaks, are run at Epsom Downs in Surrey.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom is the racecourse that hosts two of the classic races.

clue.text: Contagion, great film, half claimed

indicators.note: what is claimed is taken and held, so it goes inside

parts.note: an epic is a grand film
demi- is a prefix meaning half

explanation.surface: A review of the film Contagion calls it great, half-heartedly.
explanation.walkthrough: Contagion is also the name of a 2011 pandemic film, which makes 'great film' feel like a review, and 'half claimed' feel like an amount.
explanation.definitionFit: An epidemic is a widespread outbreak of contagious disease.

clue.text: Asian artist on question one after opening of investigation

indicators.note: after means the other pieces come after the opening letter of investigation
on means the word for artist comes just before, sitting on, the next piece
the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: only the first letter of investigation is used
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An Asian painter is quizzed, with one name put first in an inquiry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening of' gives I, and 'after' puts the rest behind it; 'on' sets RA ahead of Q in this down clue. RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of London's Royal Academy of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: An Iraqi comes from Iraq, a country in western Asia, so the word fits as a noun for an Asian person.

clue.text: War god is brave, though no leader

indicators.note: with no leader, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: someone who dares is brave enough to act

explanation.surface: A war god is courageous even without a commander at the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is brave' must be turned into a single verb form before 'no leader' takes off its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ares is the Greek god of war, the counterpart of the Roman Mars.

clue.text: Gut ain't silent when windy!

definitions.note: used as an attributive noun, as in a gut feeling or gut problem, so it matches an adjective

indicators.note: windy means winding or twisting, so the letters twist into another arrangement

explanation.surface: A joke about a bowel that is anything but quiet after a bout of wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when windy' rearranges AIN'T SILENT. The surface plays on flatulence, but windy here means twisting, like a winding road.
explanation.definitionFit: Intestinal means relating to the intestines, the bowel, which is the gut in everyday speech.

clue.text: Promise to cover rear in bikini by maiden with — this?

indicators.note: to cover means wrapping round, so the promise word wraps the other letters

parts.note: to swear is to promise

indicators.note: by means beside, so the maiden letter sits next to the bikini's last letter
rear in means the last letter of bikini

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: Someone vows to cover their backside in a bikini, with the dash pointing to the clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: IMW goes after SW. 'this' points back to the bikini, which is what the answer is.
explanation.definitionFit: A bikini is an example of swimwear, clothing worn for bathing.

clue.text: Miniature dish, it's sad to see

parts.note: wee = tiny (Scots)
a pie is a dish

explanation.surface: Someone finds a tiny pie a sorry sight.
explanation.walkthrough: A weepie is a tear-jerking film, a sad thing to see.
explanation.definitionFit: A weepie is a sentimental film that makes you cry.
